milestones.title: Marconi transatlantic transmission
milestones.citation: Dec 12, 1901 — the Morse code letter "S" transmitted from Poldhu, Cornwall and received at Signal Hill, St. John's, Newfoundland, ~3,440 km away — the first proof radio could carry beyond the horizon — history.com/this-day-in-history/december-12/marconi-sends-first-atlantic-wireless-transmission

milestones.title: KDKA Pittsburgh, first commercial broadcast
milestones.citation: Nov 2, 1920 — KDKA's Harding–Cox election-night broadcast, widely cited as the first commercially licensed radio broadcast in the United States

milestones.title: 1936 Berlin Olympics broadcast
milestones.citation: Popularly cited as the first broadcast strong enough to leak into space (the "Hitler is the first thing aliens see" story), but SETI's Seth Shostak has publicly doubted a low-power, non-directional signal of that era actually escaped the ionosphere — shown here anyway, flagged as disputed rather than silently omitted — themarysue.com/human-radio-broadcasts

milestones.title: Sputnik 1 beacon
milestones.citation: Oct 4, 1957 — Sputnik 1's radio beacon transmitted at 20.005 and 40.002 MHz for about three weeks, the first artificial signal broadcast from orbit

milestones.title: Apollo 11 moonwalk broadcast
milestones.citation: Jul 20, 1969 — the first live television broadcast of humans walking on another world, watched by an estimated 600 million people on Earth
